articles.title: Caught at Night With Girlfriend: Villagers Force Midnight Marriage in Meerut
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A dramatic incident from Meerut’s Parikshitgarh police station area has gone viral after villagers allegedly forced a young couple to marry on the spot. The incident occurred in Ikla Rasulpur village, where a youth from Mawana had arrived late at night to meet his girlfriend.

body.html:
A dramatic incident from Meerut’s Parikshitgarh police station area has gone viral after villagers allegedly forced a young couple to marry on the spot. The incident occurred in Ikla Rasulpur village, where a youth from Mawana had arrived late at night to meet his girlfriend.

According to local reports, the girl informed her boyfriend, Al Fahad, that her parents had gone to Meerut for eye treatment. Taking the opportunity, Fahad reached her house at night with his friends. However, noise from the house alerted neighbours, who caught the youth red-handed while his friends fled.

The neighbours immediately informed the girl’s family, who rushed back to the village. The family initially talked about taking legal action. The youth’s family and other relatives were then called to the spot, and a panchayat was convened in the night in the presence of villagers.

The panchayat continued for several hours, after which both sides reached a consensus to get the couple married immediately. The boy’s family reportedly asked for some time for the marriage, but the girl’s family refused and warned that they would approach the police. Following this, a Qazi was called on the spot, the girl was dressed hurriedly in bridal attire, and the marriage rituals were completed in the same night. The bride was then sent off with the groom.

A video of the incident has surfaced and is now widely discussed on social media.

articles.title: IndiGo Hit by Major Crew Shortage; 250+ Flights Cancelled Across Metro Airports #breakingnews
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: IndiGo is facing a severe crew shortage for the third straight day, with over 250 flights cancelled across Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru.

body.html:
IndiGo is facing a severe crew shortage for the third straight day, with over 250 flights cancelled across Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru. The disruption comes after DGCA’s new duty-rest rules mandating longer breaks for crew — including 48 hours rest after 7 days of work, limited night-shift landings, and 24 hours rest after long flights. Airlines may now need to hire more staff to comply with the regulations.
